chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about a man who accuses his wife falsely. He said: “He is to be flogged.” I said: “What if she pardons him?” He said: “No, and no favor.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: This report does not contradict the report of Samāʿah which indicates the permissibility of pardon, because this is to be understood to mean that she has no right to pardon after she has referred the matter to the authority and it has become known to him. Rather, she only had the right to pardon before that, as we shall explain later, if Allah wills.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانِ: the governing authority or judicial ruler
key_terms.الْعَفْوِ: pardon or remission of the claim
key_terms.عَفَتْ: she pardoned or waived her claim
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse falsely of illicit sexual conduct
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to receive flogging as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Can a wife pardon her husband after he falsely accuses her and the case reaches the authority?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal ruling for a man who falsely accuses his wife, stating that he is to be flogged. It also clarifies, through Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation, that the wife’s pardon is only valid before the matter is raised to the ruling authority, not after it reaches the السلطان.
